verdict.rationale: GrowthBook's SDKs download one cacheable JSON payload of feature definitions and evaluate flags locally, including on servers. Attribute values stay in SDK memory, and server-side experiments need no third-party requests, so the core no-network-per-check design is clearly documented. However, the 'microsecond decisions' performance claim is not evidenced, and how server SDKs cache and refresh the ruleset is documented only through the separate Proxy. Missing for 10: evidence of microsecond-level evaluation latency or benchmarks, first-party server-SDK docs on cache refresh behavior, independent hands-on corroboration of local evaluation performance.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, my server SDKs evaluate flags locally from a cached ruleset — microsecond decisions with no network call per flag check

citations.quote: With GrowthBook, there's a single cacheable JSON definition of all of the features and then evaluation happens locally within the SDKs
This evaluation happens wherever the SDK runs—in the browser, on your server, or at the edge.
They are only stored in memory locally within the SDK.
You can also run server-side experiments by using inline experiments directly with our SDK. This requires no 3rd party requests
The SDK Connection Endpoint provides readonly access to a subset of your feature flag data, just enough for the GrowthBook SDKs to assign values to users.
Run the GrowthBook Proxy next to your app to cache SDK payloads, reduce latency, and keep serving flags if the API is down.
